title: BTEC National Extended Diploma Electrical and Electronic Engineering — selected Unit 19

handoff.scope: Inventory and generation/extraction requirements only. No symbol geometry, device models, footprints or application subfolder feature is implemented.
handoff.folder_semantics: folder is a proposed slash-separated logical path, not a claim of support in the current TinyCAD library browser.
handoff.source_document_base: All source_document paths are relative to the repository root, including in standalone library files.
handoff.identity: id is stable within a library; extraction may deduplicate by canonical_symbol_id, but each library is complete and permits independent duplicate assets.
handoff.pin_contract: Logical terminal numbers and signal names are not physical package pinouts. Resolve real package pins from an authoritative device reference before generating package-specific symbols.
handoff.conventions: Prefer IEC/UK teaching symbols. Power pins and polarity should remain explicit. Built-in instruments and probes are already provided and are excluded from symbol generation.
handoff.existing_tools: existing_tools and existing_tool_ids refer to supplied non-library tools, not generation requirements. Never recreate these as library symbols.
handoff.inventory_not_bom: One record per reusable symbol type, not per component instance. A bridge can be assembled from repeated diode/resistor symbols. Different resistance/capacitance values are properties, not separate symbols.
handoff.model_warning: Every record is marked not ready to simulate from this manifest. A successful extraction of artwork does not establish a valid model, mapping or instrument implementation.
handoff.optionality: experiment_symbol_ids are a coverage set of proposed implementations and comparisons, not a minimal mandatory BOM; common support symbols and explicitly optional additions are separately identified.

experiments.title: Diode characteristic
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a limited DC sweep and collect component V/I. Compare selected signal and rectifier diode models, including the effect of the external resistor.

experiments.title: Half-wave rectification
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture a low-voltage sine input and resistive-load output. Compare polarity, conduction intervals and mean output.

experiments.title: Full-wave rectification
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw a bridge and identify which diodes conduct in each half-cycle. Compare output ripple frequency with the half-wave version.

experiments.title: Smoothing and load regulation
experiments.catalogue_description: Add a reservoir capacitor, change the load and capture ripple and mean voltage. Use transient analysis rather than a small-signal AC sweep to model rectifier conduction.

experiments.title: Zener reference/regulation
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a breakdown-capable model and a limiting resistor. Vary input and load, then compare output voltage, device current and power.

experiments.title: LED indicator design
experiments.catalogue_description: Select resistor values against a stated current target. Compare nominal and tolerance cases using the selected LED model. Brightness and damage require further modelling or measurement.

experiments.title: BJT switching
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare input drive, base current, collector current and output voltage through the switching range. Check a real model rather than imposing an unlimited current-gain assumption.

experiments.title: FET switching
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare electrical load response to gate pulses and input-voltage changes. Use the appropriate N/P-channel model and connections.

experiments.title: Transistor bias and operating point
experiments.catalogue_description: Adjust a bias network and inspect DC voltages/currents. Compare predicted and measured quiescent conditions before applying a signal.

experiments.title: Single-stage transistor amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare input/output amplitude and phase, then sweep frequency at a fixed bias. Obtain gain and bandwidth and repeat for a changed load.

experiments.title: Comparator threshold
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep one input across a reference and capture output switching. Include supply limits and a suitable comparator/op-amp model.

experiments.title: Inverting amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Change feedback ratio, compare signed gain and inspect clipping with an adequately realistic model.

experiments.title: Non-inverting amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Repeat at several gains and compare input loading, output amplitude and operating range.

experiments.title: Amplifier/filter frequency response
experiments.catalogue_description: Supply a model with frequency dependence. Compare cutoff and gain–bandwidth behaviour; use a declared active filter topology if investigating its component sensitivity.

experiments.title: Gate truth tables
experiments.catalogue_description: Test all input combinations of the specified basic gates. State logic levels, supply and the selected device family.

experiments.title: TTL/CMOS interface and timing
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare loaded output and input thresholds using compatible models. Capture propagation delay only if the models represent it. Ideal Boolean behaviour cannot establish real-family specifications.

experiments.title: Minimise and verify combinational logic
experiments.catalogue_description: Prepare alternative implementations of a function and compare their complete truth tables. Karnaugh-map reasoning remains in the student's analysis, not an automatic TinyCAD tool.

experiments.title: Latches and flip-flops
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply defined clock/data/reset sequences to prepared R-S, D or JK models. Capture state changes and distinguish asynchronous inputs from clocked inputs.

experiments.title: Counters and shift register
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare three-stage counter or register sequences. Test reset and observe ripple delays where the model supports them.

experiments.title: Simulation-to-bench comparison
experiments.catalogue_description: Produce diagrams, saved settings, labelled results and a comparison table. Diagnose differences using measured components and instrument loading, then record the resulting design changes and personal reflection.

experiments.title: Physical build/test preparation
experiments.catalogue_description: Annotate supplies, polarity, pin names and test points. The schematic supports construction and measurement; it does not prove safe soldering, assembly quality or the learner's practical performance.
